'''''Macrochloa tenacissima''''', [[Synonym (taxonomy)|synonym]] '''''Stipa tenacissima''''', ('''esparto''', '''esparto grass''', '''halfah grass''', '''alfa grass''', or '''needle grass''') is a perennial [[grass]] of northwestern [[Africa]] and the southern part of the [[Iberian Peninsula]].<ref name=IUCN/> Phylogenetic and morphological evidence indicated that the species did not belong in ''Stipa'',<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Vázquez |first1=F.M. |last2=Barkworth |first2=M.E. |title=Resurrection and emendation of ''Macrochloa'' (Gramineae: Stipeae) |journal=Botanical Journal of the Linnean Society |date=2004 |volume=144 |issue=4 |pages=483–495}}</ref><ref name="Romaschenko">{{cite book |last1=Romaschenko |first1=K. |last2=Peterson |first2=P.M. |last3=Soreng |first3=R.J. |last4=Garcia-Jacas |first4=N. |last5=Susanna |first5=A. |editor1-last=Seberg |editor1-first=Ole |editor2-last=Petersen |editor2-first=G. |editor3-last=Barfod |editor3-first=A.S. |editor4-last=Davis |editor4-first=J.I. |title=Diversity, phylogeny, and evolution in the monocotyledons |date=2010 |publisher=Aarhus Universitetsforlag |pages=511–537 |chapter=Phylogenetics of Stipeae (Poaceae: Pooideae) Based on Plastid and Nuclear DNA Sequences}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Romaschenko |first1=K. |last2=Peterson |first2=P.M. |last3=Soreng |first3=R.J. |last4=Garcia-Jacas |first4=N. |last5=Futorna |first5=O. |last6=Susanna |first6=A. |title=Systematics and evolution of the needle grasses (Poaceae: Pooideae: Stipeae) based on analysis of multiple chloroplast loci, ITS, and lemma micromorphology |journal=Taxon |volume=61 |issue=1 |pages=18–44 |doi=10.1002/tax.611002|hdl=10261/72333 |hdl-access=free }}</ref> and recent sources treat the species as ''Macrochloa tenacissima'' as a result.<ref name="powo">{{cite web |title=''Macrochloa tenacissima'' (L.) Kunth |url=https://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:407732-1 |website=Plants of the World Online |publisher=Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew |access-date=2025-08-22}}.</ref><ref>{{cite web |last1=Valdés |first1=B. |last2=Scholz |first2=H. |last3=Raab-Straube |first3=E. |last4=Parolly |first4=G. |title=Poaceae (pro parte majore) |url=https://europlusmed.org/cdm_dataportal/taxon/ad19c16d-8d72-4432-a84e-2086e635e4d3 |website=Euro+Med PlantBase - the information resource for Euro-Mediterranean plant diversity |date=2009}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last1=Krawczyk |first1=K. |last2=Mazdziarz |first2=M. |last3=Paukszto |first3=Ł. |last4=Nobis |first4=M. |last5=Sawicki |first5=J. |title=Phylogenetic reconstruction and species delimitation in Stipeae with special reference to Stipa (Poaceae, Pooideae) using mitochondrial genomes |journal=Cladistics |date=2025 |doi=10.1111/cla.12618|doi-access=free |pmc=12267929 }}</ref>

==Distribution==
[[File:Macrochloa tenacissima subsp. tenacissima kz20.jpg|thumb|left|Plants near Granada, Andalusia]]
''Macrochloa tenacissima'' is [[native species|native]] to the [[Iberian Peninsula]], the [[Balearic Islands]], and northwestern Africa ([[Morocco]], [[Algeria]], [[Tunisia]], and [[Libya]]).<ref name="powo"/> It grows in dry, sandy or rocky and base rich soils, forming a steppe-like [[grassland]]. It has been managed by people for centuries.<ref name=IUCN/>

==Description==
''Macrochloa tenacissima'' is a large grass growing to {{convert|1.5|–|2|m|ft|0}} tall with stout stems. The leaves are [[convolute (botany)|convoluted]] (rolled), {{convert|30|–|120|cm|ft|0}} long and 1 mm diameter, and with a sharp apex. The flowerheads form compact [[panicle]]s {{cvt|25|–|35|cm}} long, with [[glume]]s 1 cm long.<ref name="Thorogood">{{cite book |last=Thorogood |first=Chris |title=Field guide to the wild flowers of the western Mediterranean |publisher=Kew publishing Royal Botanic Gardens |publication-place=Richmond |date=2016 |isbn=978-1-84246-616-2 |page=145}}</ref><ref name="RHSD">{{cite book |last1=Huxley |first1=Anthony |last2=Griffiths |first2=Mark |last3=Levy |first3=Margot |title=The New Royal Horticultural Society Dictionary of Gardening |publisher=Macmillan Stockton press |publication-place=London New York |date=1992 |isbn=1-56159-001-0 |volume=4 |page=382}}</ref>

==Uses==
{{Main|Esparto}}
''Macrochloa tenacissima'' produces a fibre product called [[esparto]] which is used for crafts, such as [[Rope|cords]], [[basketry]], and [[espadrille]]s as well as for making paper.<ref name=IUCN/>

==See also==
*''[[Lygeum spartum]]'', another species of grass also used as [[esparto]].
